questions.question: What is the fundamental purpose of a clock signal in synchronous digital circuits?
options: To provide a constant power supply to all logic gates.
To synchronize the operations of all sequential elements (e.g., flip-flops and registers).
To amplify digital signals to higher voltage levels.
To control the flow of data between memory and CPU only.
To reset all circuit elements to a known state upon power-up.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of **virtual memory** in computer architecture?
options: To directly execute instructions from secondary storage without loading them into RAM.
To increase the physical clock speed of the CPU by reducing memory access times.
To allow programs to address a memory space larger than the physically available RAM, using disk space as an extension.
To provide a high-speed buffer between the CPU and the main memory (RAM).
To ensure data consistency across multiple CPU cores sharing a common memory.

questions.question: In modern ASIC/SoC design verification, what is the primary advantage of employing **constrained random verification (CRV)**?
options: It guarantees mathematical proof of correctness for all possible input sequences.
It uses pre-written, specific test vectors to thoroughly check known corner cases.
It exhaustively simulates every possible state of the design to find bugs.
It efficiently covers a wide range of scenarios and corner cases by generating varied inputs within specified valid ranges, often finding unforeseen bugs.
It automatically translates high-level specifications into hardware description language code.

questions.question: In advanced semiconductor process nodes (e.g., 28nm and below), which type of power consumption becomes increasingly dominant, even when a digital circuit is in an idle or standby state, and often requires techniques like multiple threshold voltages (multi-Vt) for mitigation?
options: Dynamic power due to switching activity.
Short-circuit power during signal transitions.
Power consumed by the clock distribution network.
Leakage power (static power) due to subthreshold conduction and gate oxide tunneling.
Power associated with I/O pad drivers and receivers.

questions.question: In modern CPU architectures, what is the primary purpose of implementing distinct **privilege levels** (or modes, e.g., kernel mode, user mode)?
options: To enable the CPU to execute multiple instructions simultaneously in parallel.
To differentiate between memory accesses from the cache and those from main memory.
To protect critical operating system resources and hardware from unauthorized access or malicious modification by user-level programs.
To optimize the power consumption of the processor based on workload demands.
To allow the CPU to dynamically switch between different instruction set architectures (ISAs).
